stem: What is the purpose of Mental Health First Aid training for community members?

options.A: Teach community members to recognize mental-health or substance-use challenges, provide initial support, and help connect the person with appropriate professional or community care.
options.B: Teach community members to diagnose psychiatric disorders and independently select definitive treatment plans.
options.C: Train nonclinicians to replace professional services by providing ongoing psychotherapy and medication management.
options.D: Teach participants to avoid responding until a licensed clinician is physically present.

rationale: Current Mental Health First Aid USA guidance describes MHFA as early-intervention training that teaches people to identify, understand, and respond to signs of mental-health or substance-use challenges, provide an initial level of support, and help connect the person with appropriate professional or other support. MHFA explicitly states that First Aiders do not diagnose mental illness and do not provide therapy or replace professional treatment. Therefore A is correct. B and C assign diagnostic/treatment roles outside the program, while D contradicts the purpose of equipping community members to offer safe initial support before or while professional help is being accessed.
educational_objective: Recognize Mental Health First Aid as an early-intervention community training program focused on recognizing challenges, providing initial support, and connecting people with appropriate help rather than diagnosing or replacing professional treatment.
source_organization: Mental Health First Aid USA / National Council for Mental Wellbeing
source_document_title: Mental Health First Aid Frequently Asked Questions; About Mental Health First Aid
source_version_date: Current MHFA USA guidance live-rechecked August 16, 2026
source_locator: FAQ: MHFA provides early support by spotting warning signs and acting before problems worsen; First Aiders/Instructors do not diagnose or provide therapy and can connect people to professional help. About MHFA: training teaches how to recognize, understand and respond to mental-health/substance-use challenges and offer the first level of support.
source_claim_supported: Mental Health First Aid trains community members to recognize and respond to mental-health/substance-use challenges, provide initial support, and connect people with appropriate help; it does not train them to diagnose or replace professional treatment.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)

source_original.rationale: Mental Health First Aid teaches participants to recognize signs of mental health or substance-use challenges, provide initial support, and help connect people with appropriate professional care. The program explicitly does not train participants to diagnose or replace professional treatment.
source_original.source_detail: MHFA teaches recognition, response, first-level support, and connection to appropriate care; First Aiders do not diagnose or replace professional help. Source has no separate formal version identifier in the cited page metadata; live currentness and applicability rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Health Promotion and Maintenance: preventive screening, age/risk-appropriate teaching, developmental and health-promotion activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained the MHFA-purpose construct and key A. Tightened the answer to current program language by specifying professional or community support and clarified in the rationale that First Aiders neither diagnose nor provide therapy; no difficulty change was needed.

audit_findings.clinical_category: Mental Health First Aid community early intervention
audit_findings.source_authority: Current Mental Health First Aid USA/National Council for Mental Wellbeing program guidance; NCSBN 2026 blueprint
audit_findings.exact_locator: MHFA FAQ early intervention, diagnosis/therapy limits, and About MHFA first-level support language
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item accurately describes the scope of the community training and does not confer diagnostic, psychotherapy, prescribing, or replacement-clinician roles on First Aiders.

distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because MHFA First Aiders do not diagnose or independently select definitive treatment.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because MHFA does not train nonclinicians to replace therapy or medication management.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because the program is designed to equip participants to provide safe initial support and connect people with help rather than wait passively for a clinician to be physically present.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A matches the program's early-intervention purpose and defined nonclinical role.
audit_findings.cueing: All options describe possible training purposes/roles; the key depends on the official program scope.
audit_findings.blueprint: Health Promotion and Maintenance — community education, early recognition and referral/support.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked current MHFA USA FAQ/About guidance, role limitations, all alternatives, rationale, objective, ambiguity, cueing and NCSBN Health Promotion alignment. A remained uniquely correct.
